title: Make game music and sound effects on your own computer
summary: A developer's add-on lets Claude Code generate, loop and export music and sound effects locally; they share unedited samples made on an M1 Mac.
agent_role: The agent turns a plain request into a sound prompt, generates candidates, picks loop lengths, trims, sets loudness and exports files; the person asks and chooses.
outcome: The author shares samples they say were generated on an M1 Mac without hand editing, and a session where Claude chose an 11-bar loop so the beat repeats cleanly.
what_they_did: A developer built a connector that gives Claude Code a local sound studio using the Stable Audio 3 model. You ask in plain words for background music or an effect. The agent generates options, loops them, evens out loudness and exports files for a game engine or video editor.
how_it_went: The author shares lo-fi, orchestral, chiptune and sound-effect samples they say were made on an M1 Mac and not edited. In one shown session, Claude picked an 11-bar loop so the beat stays in time.
worth_knowing: It needs an Apple Silicon Mac or an NVIDIA graphics card and several gigabytes of disk. On Windows you must accept the model license on Hugging Face and log in yourself.
prompt: Using my local sound generation tool, make [length]-second [style] background music at [BPM] BPM for [scene], loopable without a jump. Give me 3 candidates. Then make a sound effect of [describe the sound and the space]. Normalize loudness to [target loudness] and export as [WAV/OGG] to [folder]. Show me the options before overwriting any existing files.

curation.rationale: Mostly a tool README, but it shows a real Claude session making loopable music and publishes unedited samples with prompts and seeds; useful for game and video makers.
